name: Dopamine decor
summary: A room built for joy after the years at home of 2020 and 2021. Saturated hues drench walls, trim and ceiling; curved, inflated furniture in velvet and bouclé stands on patterned rugs; objects are personal and sorted by colour.

philosophy.core_thesis: Colour and play in the home lift the mood, and a room must show the joy of the person who lives in it.
design_principles: Drench one wall plane, with its trim and its part of the ceiling, in one saturated hue.
Use 4–6 saturated hues and repeat each hue in at least 3 places in the room.
Choose curved, pill-shaped and inflated forms with corner radii of 10 cm or more.
Lay one patterned rug, checkerboard, wave or free blob, with a repeat of 20–40 cm.
Set the strongest hue on the wall in the sightline from the entrance.
Sort books and objects by hue on the shelves, in rainbow order.
Give the lamps colour too: candy-coloured glass, acrylic and mushroom shades.
anti_patterns: Beige, grey and greige as the main palette
Straight-edged boxy furniture in neutral fabric
One accent colour on a neutral room
Bare walls without art or objects
Matching furniture sets from one range

composition.plan_logic: A colour-block plan: each zone takes its own saturated hue, and curved furniture breaks the orthogonal grid of the room.
composition.focal_point: A colour-drenched wall in the strongest hue, with a large curved sofa in a second hue in front of it.

rules.rule: Drench the back wall, its trim and its ceiling strip in the strongest hue, and set the main sofa in front of it.
Give one hue the walls, a second hue the big furniture, and 3–4 more hues the accents.
Combine hues far apart on the colour wheel at high chroma; use no neutral border.
Repeat each hue in at least 3 places, so that the room reads as one set.
Repeat a checkerboard or a wave on the rug, a cushion and a tile.
Choose oversized curved pieces: a sofa with 30 cm deep arms, a mushroom lamp 50 cm wide.
Balance by colour weight: a small hot-pink object balances a large lilac field.
Group objects by hue on shelves and tables, in rainbow order.
Put the strongest hue on the wall that the entrance faces.
rules.value: 1 drenched wall on the entrance line

rules.rule: Keep some floor free around the curved pieces; walls carry art and shelves.
Give each zone its own hue: a pink reading corner, a green desk, a blue sofa group.
Keep a route around the floating sofa and the rug.
Use coloured glass shades and one neon or coloured LED; keep the white light warm.
Shoot the room level, with a frontal view toward the drenched wall with the sofa on the right third.

zoning.circulation: A loop around a floating sofa on a free-shaped rug; routes curve with the furniture.

palette.distribution: Lilac on the drenched walls, trim and ceiling strip; tangerine on the sofa and rug; cobalt, chartreuse, hot pink and sunflower on cushions, lamps, tiles and art.

lighting.strategy: Colour is in the lamps too. Glass and acrylic shades in candy colours glow; one neon or coloured strip adds a colour wash.
lighting.daylight: Coloured curtains in the secondary hue, open by day; a saturated wall turns daylight warm or cool, so test paint at the window.

materials.finish: Gloss paint on trim and furniture; velvet and bouclé on seats. Sheens mix freely.
materials.texture_contrast: Soft rounded textiles against gloss lacquer and glass, at about 1:1.

furniture.silhouette: Curved, pill-shaped and inflated forms; chunky round legs; scalloped and wavy edges.
furniture.arrangement: Pieces float in the room on a patterned rug; a curved sofa sits free of the wall, at an angle or on a curve.
key_pieces: tufted rug in a free shape

textiles.pattern: Checkerboard, wavy stripes and free blobs at 20–40 cm repeats; 2–3 patterns in one room, each in the room hues.
textiles.windows: Coloured curtains in the secondary hue, or bare windows with a painted frame.

objects.approach: Personal and joyful: colourful ceramics, pop art prints, glass in candy colours, collected souvenirs.
objects.grouping: Group by hue in rainbow order; 3–7 objects per shelf; a gallery wall of 5–9 frames.

implementation.brief: A lilac room, drenched from wall to trim to ceiling strip. A curved tangerine velvet sofa floats on a checkerboard rug; a cobalt chair, a chartreuse side table, a mushroom lamp and a wavy mirror complete the group.
implementation.image_prompt: Dopamine decor living room, lilac colour-drenched walls and trim, curved tangerine velvet sofa, checkerboard rug in pink and orange, cobalt blue armchair, chartreuse gloss side table, glass mushroom lamp, wavy mirror with a sunflower frame, colour-sorted bookshelf, pop art prints, playful maximalist, bright warm light, editorial interior photograph
implementation.negative_prompt: Beige, grey, greige, boxy neutral furniture, minimal empty room, cool white light, wood grain, matching set.
implementation.camera: 24 mm lens, camera at 130 cm, frontal view toward the drenched wall with the sofa on the right third.
implementation.scene_3d: Room 550 x 450 cm, ceiling 260 cm. Warm 3000 K ambient from a glass pendant; 2 table lamps; one magenta emissive strip at 1500 nits; walls with saturated paint.

emotion.target_response: A lift of the mood: the viewer smiles and feels energy, play and permission to like colour.

avoid_when: The brief asks for rest, sleep or concentration.
The room must suit many users with unknown taste, such as a rental.

modifiers.how: Change velvet to printed laminate, add squiggle and grid patterns and sharp primary solids; keep 4–6 saturated hues.
Paint the walls white, keep one hue for 5% accents, change velvet to wool; keep the curved forms.

canonical_works.work: The Gallery at Sketch, London (pink scheme)

sources.title: Ingrid Fetell Lee, Joyful: The Surprising Power of Ordinary Things to Create Extraordinary Happiness (Little, Brown Spark, 2018)
Trend evidence, cite only: the term spread on short-video and image platforms from 2021
